chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one person, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
What the snare seizes and cuts off something from it, that is dead (impermissible to eat); but what you find of the rest of its body still alive, slaughter it (Islamically) and then eat from it.

key_terms.الحبالة: The snare or trap used in hunting, a device that catches animals without involving direct human slaughter
key_terms.فذكه: Command to perform tadhkiya (Islamic slaughter) — slitting the throat with mention of God's name, which makes an animal permissible
key_terms.ميت: Dead/mayta — an animal that has died without proper Islamic slaughter, considered ritually impure and forbidden to eat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating an animal caught by a snare in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a jurisprudential ruling on hunting with a snare or trap. If the snare kills the animal by severing a part, the severed part is treated as mayta (unlawfully killed carrion) and is forbidden to eat. However, if any part of the animal's body is still alive when retrieved, it must be slaughtered according to Islamic rites (tadhkiya) to render it permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia fiqh principle that the method of slaughter determines the permissibility of meat.
